title: ELECTION DAY
full_story:
Election Day is tomorrow and 1.16 million early ballots have already been turned in.

Ballots cast in the election come from two sources, mail-in voting and early in-person voting.  The total number of in person votes was about 608,000.  Mail ballots returned were about 556,000 – less than half of requested mail-in ballots.

A gubernatorial race is on the ballot this year with incumbent Governor JB Pritzker facing Republican challenger Darren Bailey.

In addition to governor, voters will see these state offices on their ballot, attorney general, secretary of state, comptroller and treasurer, in the Illinois Senate; 39 of the 59 seats, and in the Illinois House of Representatives all 118 seats.

At the federal level, Democrat Juliana Stratton, Republican Don Tracy and Independent Whitfield Harrington Jr. are competing for the US Senate seat being vacated by retiring Senator Dick Durbin.  Voters also will elect representatives in all 17 Illinois congressional districts.

On the Clay County ballot voters will choose between incumbent representative Mike Bost and challenger Julie Fortier.  There is also a race for a member of the Clay County Board in District K between David E. Johnson and Rachel Walker.  There will also be Judicial Retention questions on the ballot.

For a ballot preview voters should visit the county clerk’s website, where specimen ballots are typically posted before Election Day.

Eligible residents can still register during early voting or on Election Day November 3rd at their polling locations, open from 6 am to 7 pm.

title: LOUISVILLE FALL FESTIVAL ROYALTY
full_story:
The Louisville Fall Festival crowned its royalty on Saturday afternoon.

The 2026 Miss Louisville Fall Festival is Laila Smith, the daughter of Dustin and Kathy Smith of Louisville.  Laila was sponsored by the Serene & Silk Boutique.  There were 6 contestants running for Queen.  The retiring Queen was Mila Zink.

The Junior Miss is Chloe Schnepper, sponsored by ELT Transport.  There were 7 girls in the Junior Miss Pageant.  The retiring JR Miss is Elsie Anderson.

The new Little Miss is Eveleigh Bailey, sponsored by Glamour Farms.  There were 10 young ladies in the Little Miss Pageant.  The retiring Little Miss is Landrey Eade.

title: FLORA PARADE WINNERS
full_story:
Winners were named in the Flora Halloween Parade held Saturday night.

Winning 1st place for horses, youth, was Sophia Hosselton, 2nd place went to Paityn Waters.  Winning 1st place for horses, adults, was Jennifer Davis, 2nd place Ashley Hosselton, and 3rd Place Ethan McAllister.  Anthony McAllister took first place in the Mule category.

Winning 1st place in the floats category was the float from ACT Tire and Auto.  2nd place was awarded to Daszle Dance and Tumble, and 3rd prize was awarded to the Clay County Coon Hunters Club.

In the Industry Non Float category AAA Disposal took 1st place, Rogers Heating and Air was 2nd, and Prairie Central Trucking was 3rd.

In classic cars the winners were Ryan Beard 1st, 2nd place went to Ivan Barnett, and 3rd place went to the Betty Olden.

The top band was the North Wayne Band, followed by the Floyd Henson JR High band and the Flora High School Band.

In the Side by Side Category 1st place went to the Village Mudbugs.

title: VETERANS BREAKFASTS
full_story:
Clay County Schools will be honoring Veterans on Monday, November 9th and Tuesday, November 10th.

The Flora School District will be hosting its annual Veterans’ Day program on Monday, November 9th.  There will be breakfast at 8:15 am in the Flora High School Commons for all veterans and their families.  A program, open to anyone in the community, will follow in the Conley Gymnasium.  The program will consist of performances by elementary, junior high, and high school students and a keynote address by a local veterans.  Everyone is invited to honor the dedication and service of our veterans.  Please call 618-662-2412 to let the school know how many will be attending the breakfast so proper arrangements can be made.

North Clay Unit 25 will also be having a Veterans Day program on Tuesday, November 10th.  The Veterans Breakfast will be served at 8 am in the North Clay Commons.  To make reservations for breakfast call Kali Carroll at 618-665-3393 extension 135 or email [email protected] so proper arrangements can be made.  The Veterans program will be at 9 am in the Clay County State Bank Arena.

Clay City Schools will hold a Veterans Day breakfast and assembly on Monday, November 9th.  All veterans and their families are invited to join the festivities for breakfast from 7:45 to 8:45 am with a program to follow at 9 am.  To confirm your attendance, please call the Clay City Schools at 618-676-1431.

Cisne FFA plans to honor local Veterans during their 2nd Veterans Day Breakfast on Monday from 7:30-9:30 am at the Cisne Community Center.  The complimentary breakfast includes pancakes, sausage, scrambled eggs, fruit-salad, biscuits & gravy, coffee, juice, milk.  They Welcome Wayne and Clay County Veterans and encourage them to bring family or guests.  Learn more by calling or texting Mikkie Hearle at 618-516-3371.

title: LEAF COLLECTION UNDERWAY
full_story:
The City of Flora Department of Public Works fall curbside leaf collection will begin Sunday.  City residents should have their loose leaves to the curbside on their normal scheduled leaf collection day.  Please keep in mind that the crew may run behind schedule during this time, and they appreciate your patience and understanding.  To help crews more efficiently collect leaves, please remember the following, rake leaves in wind rows, a long narrow line, rather than piles next to the curb.  Also, the City will not pick up anything in the alley.

Keep wind rows as close to the curb as possible but do not rake leaves into the street.  This is in violation of a city ordinance and will plug the storm sewers.

Keep wind rows away from trees, hydrants, signposts, electrical pedestals, or other obstacles.

Keep all garbage, metal, branches, and sticks out of the wind rows.

Do not park vehicles next to the leaf wind rows.  If they can’t get the vacuum to the wind rows, they will have to wait until your next collection day.

As a reminder this is a 2-person operation so wind rows must be narrow & close to the curb.  Bulky limbs and cuttings from trees and shrubs must be cut into four-foot lengths and tied into bundles not more than two feet in diameter.  Wood and brush should not be placed in a container or garbage can.  Please place this directly on the curb.  All property owners are responsible for disposing of entire trees that are left at the shoulder for collection.  Please work with the City in keeping these guidelines in mind when cleaning up your yard this fall.  If you have any questions, please call the Department of Public Works office at 618-662-4625.

Remember that weather may slow down the leaf picker.  The vacuum will not work if the leaves are extremely wet or if it is snowing.

title: ILLINOIS BASIN CELEBRATION
full_story:
The Illinois Basin Celebration is making its return to Oblong Wednesday, bringing together local oil industry professionals for a day of networking, education, and community outreach.

Organizers say all regional oil industry professionals are invited to Wednesday’s event, which kicks off in the morning with complimentary coffee and donuts, followed by a catered lunch.  Attendees will also walk away with free “IllinoisBasinProud” swag, including stocking caps and coffee tumblers.

This year’s core focus centers strictly on workplace safety.  Starting at 8:30 am, industry workers can attend non-mandatory, hour-long safety workshops.  Mark Weiler will host a session on general oilfield safety, while Illinois Eastern Community Colleges instructor Wes Taylor will lead training on H2S and CPR.

The celebration is also opening its doors to the next generation.  The Illinois Petroleum Resources Board will host museum tours and “Petro Pros” educational presentations.  Twenty-five students from Oblong Junior High School will visit on November 4th, followed by 23 students from Hutsonville High School and Newton St. Thomas Grade School on November 5th.

Local operators and industry professionals who want to participate in the school presentations or bring out oilfield equipment to show the students are highly encouraged to get involved.

If you plan to attend the lunch, organizers ask that you message them or reply to their announcement email to reserve your seat.  More than 40 professionals have already RSVP’d, and everyone who signs up ahead of time will be entered into a drawing for a 250-dollar gift card.

title: FRAN CARTER SCHOLARSHIP FASHION SHOW
full_story:
The Frontier Community College Foundation and Carnaby Square, Fairfield’s “Fashion Leader” are once again teaming up to host the 9th Annual Fran Carter Memorial Scholarship Fashion Show on Sunday.

This event is being held at First Christian Church in Fairfield.  “All three entities were close to Fran’s heart, so it is fitting that the church work with the Foundation and Carnaby Square to host the event.”  Doors will open at 2 pm, with the fashion show beginning at 2:30 pm.  Those coming to the fashion show are asked to bring canned goods.

The fashion show highlights fall fashions available exclusively at Carnaby Square as well as tuxedos available for rental.  All tickets must be purchased in advance.  Reserved tables of 8 sell for $100 and individual tickets are available for $15 each.  Drinks and light refreshments will be served.  Tickets can be purchased exclusively at Carnaby Square or through Linda Spicer who can be reached at 217-725-1340.  All proceeds will go the Fran Carter Memorial Scholarship available to second-year student athletes at Frontier.

title: GET COVERED UNDERWAY
full_story:
Get Covered Illinois kicked off the 2027 annual open enrollment period yesterday, helping Illinoisans compare plans, apply for financial help and enroll in coverage.  With federal changes signed into law by President Trump affecting access to affordable health insurance, the state’s official marketplace is committed to connecting Illinoisans to high-quality, affordable health coverage.

“Whether enrolling for the first time or insured for years, people deserve to understand their options and feel confident in their choice,” said Ann Gillespie, Director of the Illinois Department of Insurance.  “That’s why having a marketplace dedicated to Illinoisans matters.  We know the communities we serve, the challenges they face and the importance of having reliable health coverage.  Get Covered Illinois gives residents a trusted place to make informed decisions about their coverage.”

Open enrollment runs through January 15th, giving residents the opportunity to enroll in, renew or change their health insurance.  In its second year as a state-based marketplace, Get Covered Illinois continues to deliver on its “Here to Help” mission by putting Illinoisans first.  The marketplace connects residents to coverage for the care they need, from routine checkups to ongoing treatment.

One way Illinoisans can make the most of open enrollment is by comparing plans to find coverage that meets their needs and budget.  Last year, people who shopped and compared plans saved an average of $150 a month on their premium.  With plans and prices changing each year, it’s important to review all options.  At GetCoveredIllinois.gov, Illinoisans can compare plans and estimated costs before creating an account or applying.  The website makes it easy to view premiums and deductibles, check prescription coverage and see whether preferred doctors and hospitals are in-network.  Get Covered Illinois is also the only place to apply for federal tax credits that lower the cost of coverage.

“The most important step returning customers can take is to review and compare the new plans available to them,” said Morgan Winters, Director of Get Covered Illinois.  “Do not assume last year’s plan is still the best fit.  Our licensed brokers can help you compare plans and prices and recommend a plan that fits your needs, at no cost to you.  Open enrollment is also the time to make sure the information on your application is up to date to ensure you get the correct financial help.”

Federal changes under H.R. 1 will affect some Illinoisans’ Medicaid and marketplace eligibility.  Last month, more than 9,000 lawfully present immigrants were kicked off Medicaid.  To help them avoid a gap in health insurance, Get Covered Illinois launched a special enrollment period offering retroactive coverage through December 31st.  Access to premium tax credits for this group will end on January 1st.

Get Covered Illinois is contacting impacted customers and encouraging them to carefully read their notices and reach out for help if they need it.  More information about these federal changes and when they take effect is available at GetCoveredIllinois.gov/MarketplaceChanges.

Get Covered Illinois certified navigators, trained professionals who provide free enrollment assistance, can guide Illinoisans through the application process, with support available in multiple languages.  Navigators are available to meet in person, online or over the phone in many communities across the state.  Navigators can also connect residents who are no longer eligible for Medicaid or marketplace financial help to free or low-cost health care in their community.

The annual Get Covered Illinois open enrollment period ends on January 15th.  Illinoisans who enroll by December 15th will have coverage starting January 1st.  Those who enroll by January 15th will have coverage starting February 1st.  To compare plans, enroll or find free help, visit GetCoveredIllinois.gov or call 1-866-311-1119 (TTY: 711).
